confidentiality.description: How far the deck may travel. Prints nothing by itself: footer.confidentiality decides whether the mark goes on the cover or also on every content page. "public" never prints a mark.

classification.description: A legal classification and its term, written exactly as given (e.g. "秘密★1年"). Prints on the cover only, top left. Cannot be combined with footer.confidentiality.

branding.description: Where the brand logo appears. Omitted equals "cover-only": cover and chapter pages keep the logo, content and ending pages carry none. "full" and "minimal" keep the logo on every page. "full" also paints the date on cover and ending meta rows, and without a footer object it stands for footer {organization, confidentiality: "footer"}. Page marks such as page numbers live in footer. Layout branding:"none" still wins. Theme motifs are unaffected.

page_number.description: Print the page number on content pages, bottom right. Cover, chapter and ending pages carry none. Exported as PowerPoint's own slide-number field.

organization.description: Print meta.organization on content pages, bottom left. Requires meta.organization.

label.description: The author's own occasion-and-date line, printed as written after the organization, e.g. "2026 年中期业绩 | 2026.08" or "Investor Presentation | February 2026".

notice.description: The author's own copyright line or disclaimer pointer, printed as written after the label.

draft.description: The author's own draft or version mark, e.g. "讨论稿" or "Draft for discussion", printed bottom right before the page number.

confidentiality.description: Where the meta.confidentiality mark goes. "cover" prints it once on the cover. "footer" prints it on the cover and bottom right on every content page. Requires meta.confidentiality other than "public".

footer.description: Small marks printed in the page corners. Omitted, the deck prints none. Every text is the author's own or comes from meta.

label.description: The stage as the strip names it, in a few characters, such as "环节一", "小测一" or "Part 1".

quiz.description: Marks a stage where the room checks what it has learned, such as a quiz or a test: its pill is drawn dashed.

stages.description: Two to 8 stages in the order the talk runs through them.

course.description: The stages a talk runs through in order, such as the parts and quizzes of a lesson: { "stages": [{ "label": "目标" }, { "label": "环节一" }, { "label": "小测一", "quiz": true }] }. Each page names its own stage. Drawn only by faces that have a place for a page's stage: validate says which.

ballot.description: A ballot laid over the page's items, so a committee can vote on each one: the boxes each item can be ticked in, and an optional line left blank to sign. Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

tag.description: A small tag set with the page's heading, saying what the whole page rests on, such as "RCT · NEJM 2025 · 751 例" or "Draft for comment, June 2026". Give it an evidence kind to colour it by its source. Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

ballot.description: A ballot laid over the page's items, so a committee can vote on each one: the boxes each item can be ticked in, and an optional line left blank to sign. Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

tag.description: A small tag set with the page's heading, saying what the whole page rests on, such as "RCT · NEJM 2025 · 751 例" or "Draft for comment, June 2026". Give it an evidence kind to colour it by its source. Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

ballot.description: A ballot laid over the page's items, so a committee can vote on each one: the boxes each item can be ticked in, and an optional line left blank to sign. Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

tag.description: A small tag set with the page's heading, saying what the whole page rests on, such as "RCT · NEJM 2025 · 751 例" or "Draft for comment, June 2026". Give it an evidence kind to colour it by its source. Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

ballot.description: A ballot laid over the page's items, so a committee can vote on each one: the boxes each item can be ticked in, and an optional line left blank to sign. Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

tag.description: A small tag set with the page's heading, saying what the whole page rests on, such as "RCT · NEJM 2025 · 751 例" or "Draft for comment, June 2026". Give it an evidence kind to colour it by its source. Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

Kicker.description: A short label set over the heading, such as the occasion on a cover ("Investment committee") or what an ending asks for ("For decision"). Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

label.description: The line's label, such as "致", "To" or "Signed".

value.description: What the line says, such as "全体员工" or "All staff".

note.description: A short aside after the value, such as the date beside a signature.

Fields.description: One to four header lines a document form prints, each a label and its value: To, From, Date and Re on a memo's cover, or Signed, Drafted and Copied to under its decision. Drawn only by faces that have a place for them: validate says which.

text.description: The stamp's words, such as "已决定" or "Approved". Keep them to a few characters.

date.description: A line under the words, such as "2026 · 10".

Stamp.description: A stamp pressed on the page, such as "已决定" or "Approved", with an optional date line under it. Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

choices.description: The boxes each item can be ticked in, in order, such as ["同意", "不同意", "弃权"] or ["For", "Against", "Abstain"].

signature.description: The label of a line left blank to sign under the items, such as "委员会主任委员签字" or "Chair's signature".

item_choices.description: Items whose boxes differ from choices, such as a pick among options: [{ "item": 3, "choices": ["自投", "EMC", "融资租赁"] }].

text.description: A few words for the tag, such as "改为区间", "新增" or "Unchanged". Keep it short: it is printed whole on one line.

quiet.description: Marks a tag that says nothing changed, such as 不变 or Unchanged: it steps back in a grey outline.

evidence.description: What kind of source the tag names, outlined in the ink the theme keeps for it: "trial" for a trial or a study published in a peer-reviewed journal, "label" for a product's approved label, "company" for a company's own figures, "press" for a press report, "draft" for a draft out for comment, "official" for a government or regulator's document, "registry" for a trial registry, "preprint" for a working paper or a preprint no journal has reviewed yet.

settled.description: Marks a tag whose verdict is final, such as 纳入, 不纳入 or Approved, against one still open or conditional, such as 暂缓 or Case by case: it is filled instead of outlined, in the emphasis colour, or in grey on a quiet tag.

tone.description: What kind of news the tag says, outlined in the theme's own colour for it: "danger" for a breach or a risk, such as 超说明书 or Off-label, "warning" for something to watch, "success" for something that went right.

basis.description: What it rests on, so a reader knows how firm it is: "law" for a provision in force, which the tag cites; "estimate" for a figure worked out under a stated assumption, not published and not a forecast; "pending" for a figure or item still to be confirmed or filled in; "proposal" for a rule proposed or still negotiated, not yet law.

Tone.description: What kind of news the item is, painted in the theme's own colour for it: "danger" for something that broke, "warning" for something to watch or still being handled, "success" for something that recovered or went right.

from.description: The first year of the run, such as 2026.

to.description: The last year of the run, such as 2034.

marked.description: The years this page is about, lit on the strip, such as [2026, 2027]. Each lies between from and to.

Years.description: The run of years a deck follows and the years this page is about, drawn as a strip of years with those years lit: { "from": 2026, "to": 2034, "marked": [2026, 2027] }. At most 13 years. Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

Stage.description: Which stage of the deck's course this page belongs to, written as its label, such as "环节一" or "Part 1". Requires the deck's course. Drawn only by faces that have a place for it: validate says which.

title.description: A short bold line over the text, naming what the note is about, such as "谁付" or "Who pays".

tag.description: A few words that say what the note rests on, printed as a small tag under its text, such as "企业口径 · 据报道" or "Ours after verification". Give it a basis or an evidence kind to say how firm it is.

IconName.description: One icon name from the bundled catalog. Run `pptwise icons` for the full list.

title.description: A name for the listing, printed in its title bar, such as a file name: "postmortems / quotes.txt" or "deploy.yaml".

highlight_lines.description: The lines the page is about, counted from 1, such as [11, 12]. They are set bold in the theme's warning colour.

note.description: One short line of context: the base, the period, or the counts behind the figure. Where it came from belongs in source.

tag.description: What the figure is, as a small tag, such as 约束性指标 or Binding. Filled in the emphasis colour on the marked figure.

delta_good.description: Whether the delta is good news. Unset: up is good, down bad.

title.description: A short name for the chart, printed over it, such as "参保职工与离退休人员之比" or "Workers per retiree". A theme that numbers its figures prints it after the figure's number.

chart_type.description: How to plot the series. bar/line: categories on one axis, for trends or comparisons. stacked: each category's series piled into one column with its total printed above (two or more series, negatives pile down from zero). percent_stacked: the same piles scaled to 100%, to compare make-up rather than size (two or more series, no negatives, every category above zero). combo: bars and lines on one category axis for two measures over one period, such as revenue and margin. Mark each line series `plot: "line"`, the rest are bars, at least one of each. `axis: "right"` gives a series its own right-hand scale, titled by axes.y2_title / axes.y2_unit. scatter: a numeric x-y point cloud (a per-point `size` makes bubbles); a category x takes line or bar. area: a line filled down to the baseline, for volume or a running total. pie: part-to-whole share. donut: the ring form of pie (`center_total: true` prints the total in the middle). funnel: one value narrowing across ordered stages. dumbbell: a from→to change per row. gauge: ONE value's progress toward a target as a half-ring with the number centred, such as 62% of goal. Several headline metrics side by side are `kpi_cards`, never a row of gauges.

direction.description: bar: "horizontal" lays the bars on their side. stacked: "horizontal" draws one whole as a single share bar across the page, every series one part with its one value at the chart's one category, whose name captions the bar.

y_unit.description: The unit the values are counted in, after each tick of the value axis ("%", "千"). A pie, a donut and a funnel have no axis and print it after every value they name ("1200 个", "30%").

tag.description: A few words over the chart saying what kind of figures it draws, such as 企业口径 or "Company figures", printed as a small tag at the start of its legend row. Give it an evidence kind to colour it by its source. Not on a share bar.

changes.description: Up to three changes between two of the chart's bars, each printed as a figure: a relative change ("+11%"), or points when the value axis is in percent. Without `at`, from and to name two categories (x values) and the change is bracketed over their columns: each category carries one bar, or the chart is stacked. With `at`, from and to name two series compared at that category, the change set beside the later bar. A change ending on the marked series takes the lead colour. Bar and stacked charts only.

bands.description: Up to two value ranges marked across the plot behind the data, such as a target range a line should stay in. Each runs from `from` to `to` on the value axis, which grows to hold it, and may carry a short `label`. line, area and bar charts only. Write a range this way rather than as two flat series at its edges.

from.description: Where the range starts on the value axis.

label.description: What the range is, printed in it, such as "2026 年目标区间 4.5%—5%" or "Target range".

emphasis_label.description: One line a share bar states for its marked parts, in the author's words, such as what they add up to: "第 73 章制品 €93.5 亿，占 69.5%" or "Downstream goods €9.35bn, 69.5%". It replaces the total the bar would compute. A share bar (stacked, direction "horizontal") with at least one marked series only.

reference.description: One value drawn as a dashed line across the bars, such as a benchmark, an average or a threshold the bars are read against: { "value": 1.37, "label": "EU benchmark 1.370" }. The value axis grows to hold it, and its label names the line in the legend. Bar charts only, upright or on their side. Write a benchmark this way rather than as a bar of its own.

value.description: Where the line stands on the value axis.

label.description: What the value is, such as "欧盟基准 1.370" or "EU benchmark 1.370".

markers.description: Up to three dashed lines drawn down a line chart where a category begins, such as the ages a rule changes at: [{ "before": "50-54 岁", "label": "女 50 岁" }]. Each stands halfway between the category it names and the one before it, its label over the plot. Line charts only, on a category that is not the first.

before.description: The category the line stands before, halfway between it and the one before it, such as "50-54 岁" or "Age 50-54".

label.description: What happens there, printed over the line, such as "女 50 岁" or "Women, 50".

gaps.description: Places kept for categories with no published value, such as a year a survey skipped: [{ "after": "2017", "x": "2018", "label": "未公布" }]. Upright bar and line charts only.

after.description: The category it follows, such as "2017".

x.description: Its name on the axis, such as "2018".

label.description: What it says, such as "未公布" or "Not published".

status.description: A value that is not a reported figure. "forecast" is an estimate of what will happen: its bar is hatched, and a lone bar's label says it is a forecast. "target" is a level a plan calls for: its bar is drawn as a dashed outline. "estimate" is a value worked out, not published: pale in a dashed outline. Bar and stacked charts only.

emphasis.description: Marks the one bar the page is about, such as the latest year in a run of years. It keeps its series' colour and the other bars step back. On a stacked or percent_stacked chart it marks the column the point stands in: that column keeps its colours and the other columns step back. One point per chart, on a bar, stacked or percent_stacked chart (not a share bar), and not together with a series' own emphasis.

note.description: A few words printed with the value, such as "基准线", "低约 37%" or "62.36 元": after the value of a bar on its side or a share bar's part, and beside a point of a line, such as "最低" on its lowest year or "回升" on the year it recovers. Bars on their side (bar with direction "horizontal"), the parts of a share bar and lines only.

icon.description: A symbol set before the category's name. Bars on their side only, on the first series.

upper.description: The high end when a value is only known as a range, with y its low end: y 60 and upper 70 for "60% to 70%", or y 1.8 and upper 24.2 for rates that run from 1.8% to 24.2% across 108 models. The bar is drawn solid to y and dashed on to upper, and its label names both ends. Bars on their side (bar with direction "horizontal") only.

plot.description: combo only: "line" draws this series as a line over the bars, and omitted or "bar" draws it as bars.

axis.description: combo only: "right" reads this series against its own right-hand axis (for a second unit, such as a rate beside amounts), and omitted or "left" shares the left axis.

emphasis.description: Marks the one series the page is about. It keeps the lead color and the others turn grey. At most one series, on bar, line, area, scatter, stacked, percent_stacked or combo charts with two or more series. A marked combo line also prints its values. A share bar (a stacked chart with direction "horizontal") may mark a run of adjacent parts, and states the run's total and share under it.

steps.description: scatter only: joins the series' points as steps, each value held until the next point and then jumping to it, such as a statutory age by date of birth or a rate by income band. Write the points in order of x, one where each step begins. The points are not dotted.

tone.description: What kind of news the series is, drawn in the colour every theme keeps for it: "success" for the share that got better, "danger" for the share that got worse, "warning" for one to watch. Use it when a series is good or bad news by what it counts, such as the people whose burnout fell beside those whose pace rose. On bar, line, area, scatter, stacked, percent_stacked or combo charts, not a share bar.

title.description: A short name for the timeline, printed over it, such as "2026 年外部融资" or "Funding in 2026". A theme that sets it in a panel prints the title in the panel's title bar.

lanes.description: The names of the two lanes the milestones run on, the first lane first, such as ["Home", "Abroad"]. Optional: without it the lane a milestone names first is the first lane. Every milestone's lane must be one of them. Where a theme sets the lanes on two sides of the axis, the first lane stands above it.

periods.description: Up to three spans the axis is divided into, each named with its label, such as the year imports are only counted and the year certificates are bought: [{ "from": "2026-01", "to": "2026-12", "label": "2026: counted, nothing to buy" }]. Write from and to the way the milestones write their dates. A horizontal timeline only.

from.description: Where the span starts, written the way the milestones write their dates, such as 2026-01 or 2026.

to.description: Where it ends, such as 2026-12 or 2034.

label.description: What the span is, printed with it, such as "2026 年：进口计入排放，不必持有证书" or "Current law: free allocation ends in 2034".

basis.description: What the span rests on, such as "proposal" for one that exists only if a proposal passes, or "law" for one the law sets. A span that is not settled is drawn dashed.

icon.description: A symbol for the milestone, drawn in its node on the axis, such as server or flag. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

status.description: "pending" for a milestone that has not come to pass, such as a survey round carried out whose data is not out yet: its node is drawn hollow.

tag.description: A few words that say where the milestone stands, printed as a small tag with it, such as "已定", "谈判中" or "Proposal". Give it a basis to say how firm it is: "proposal" for a rule not yet law.

source.description: Where the date or the rule comes from, printed small under the milestone, such as the act that sets it: "实施条例 (EU) 2025/2621" or "COM(2025) 989".

lane.description: The track this milestone belongs to, such as "Home" and "Abroad". The milestones keep one time order across both lanes. The ordinary timeline sets them in one row and prints each milestone's lane on a line of its own over its date. Bulletin, clinic, ledger, swiss and vermilion set a timeline on lanes across the page when it fits there, the first lane above the axis and the second below it, and the timeline's lanes field says which lane is first. Every milestone names a lane, or none does. At most two lanes.

title.description: A short name for the comparison, printed over it, such as "三个方案" or "Three options". A theme that sets it in a panel prints the title in the panel's title bar.

label_column.description: The header over the rows' labels, saying what they are, such as "药品" or "Option". Without it that header stays empty.

icon.description: A symbol for the row, drawn before its label, such as pill or server. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

tag.description: What happened to this row, in a few words printed as a small tag after its cells, such as 改为区间, 不变 or 换指标. Set quiet on a tag that says nothing changed.

emphasis.description: Marks the one row the page is about: it sits on a pale tint of the emphasis colour and its tag fills in that colour. At most one row.

tag_column.description: The header over the rows' tags, such as "变化" or "Change". Only with tags.

recommended.description: Index into columns (0 is the first) of the one option the page recommends. Its header and cells are set bold in the primary color.

recommended_label.description: A few words printed as a filled tag over the recommended option, saying who it is for or why, such as "客服用这个" or "For support teams". Only with recommended.

title.description: A short name printed over the cards, such as "按什么做".

tag.description: A few words that place the card, printed as a small tag on it, such as where or when the item comes from: Azure 2026-02. Set quiet on a tag that should step back.

icon.description: A symbol for the step, drawn in its badge where its number would stand, such as ruler or ban. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

tone.description: What kind of step it is, painted in the theme's own colour for it: "danger" for a check that can stop the process there, "warning" for one to watch, "success" for one that confirms it can go on.

icon.description: A symbol for the item, drawn between its number and its title, such as pill or hospital. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

emphasis.description: Marks the one item the page lands on, such as the answer the other items lead to. Its card is filled in the primary colour. At most one item.

icon.description: A symbol for the phase, drawn where its number would stand, such as shield-check or flag. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

basis.description: What the row's value rests on, such as "pending" for a budget line still to be set ("核算与核查费用：待定"). A value that is not settled is marked dashed.

duration.description: How long the phase lasts, counted in the roadmap's duration_unit, such as 15. Give every phase one, and a face that lays phases to scale draws each as long as it lasts.

checkpoint.description: A check held as the phase ends, such as "小测一", "Quiz 1" or "Gate review", marked where the phase ends and named on its card.

points.description: What the phase covers, one to three short lines, such as ["四项研究", "两种帮倒忙"] or ["Four studies", "Two traps"], printed as a short list on its card.

emphasis.description: Marks the one phase the page is about. Its card keeps the accent bar and the others turn primary. At most one item.

duration_unit.description: The unit every phase's duration is counted in, such as "分钟", "min", "weeks" or "个月". Required once the phases carry a duration.

title.description: A short name for the grid, printed over it, such as "已有证据覆盖了什么" or "What the evidence covers". A theme that numbers its tables prints the number before it.

columns.description: The columns' names, printed over them, one a column, such as ["就业效应", "去向", "机制"] or ["Employment", "Where they went", "Why"]. As many as cols.

rows.description: The rows' names, printed at their left, one a row, each with an optional symbol: [{ "label": "Reforms abroad", "icon": "globe" }]. As many as the grid has rows.

label.description: The row's name, such as "国际改革评估" or "Reforms abroad".

icon.description: A symbol for the row, drawn before its name, such as globe. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

empty.description: Marks a cell where nothing has been found, such as a gap in the evidence: it is drawn as a dashed outline with its words in the middle ("空白", "Nothing yet"), not on a tint. With tone "accent" the outline takes the accent, as the gap a page is about.

icon.description: A symbol for the panel, drawn before its title, such as receipt or scale. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

Crop.description: The part of the picture to keep when it is cropped to its frame: [left, top, width, height], each a fraction of the whole picture.

icon.description: A symbol drawn before the picture's caption, such as zap or map-pin. Only with a caption. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

tag.description: A few words on the picture, such as "选配" or "Optional".

image_grid.description: A 2-8 photo/screenshot grid with cover-crop cells.

title.description: Optional one-line label above the grid, e.g. what the set of organizations has in common.

name.description: The organization's name. Always required: it is the picture's alt text, the wordmark drawn when no picture is given, and the only part that survives without the asset.

asset_id.description: Optional asset id for this organization's mark, resolved through the same image pipeline as image/image_grid. Omit it and the tile sets the name as a wordmark instead.

items.description: 4-12 organizations, one per tile, in the order the wall should read row by row. Each tile holds a picture or the name set as a wordmark, nothing else.

logo_wall.description: Sets 4-12 organization marks on one grid of tiles of equal size and weight, so the page says 'these names are together' and nothing more. Use logo_wall when the set of names IS the claim — customers, partners, sponsors, funders, accreditations. The test: would each tile be replaced by that organization's own logo file? If each name needs a line of its own explaining what it did, use `row_cards` or `icon_cards`; if the pictures are photographs rather than marks, use `image_grid`.

asset_id.description: Required asset id for this item's picture, resolved through the same image pipeline as image/image_grid. A card without a picture is a row_cards row.

note.description: Optional one line saying what it does or who it is for. One line, not a paragraph.

price.description: Optional price as written, currency symbol included — "¥68", "$1,200", "12万".

price_unit.description: Optional small print beside the price — "per seat / month", "起 / 年".

featured.description: Optional. Marks the one item the page is steering toward: its card is filled solid and its text set to read against that fill. At most one item in the set may set it.

items.description: 2-4 items side by side, each a picture with a name and usually a price, in the order they should be read left to right.

product_cards.description: Puts 2-4 purchasable things side by side, each with its own picture, name, and usually a price, so the page reads as a range to choose from. A picture is required on every item. Use product_cards for a catalogue page: plans, packages, models, editions. The test: could someone buy exactly one of these? Use `comparison` when the same attributes are weighed across options without pictures, `data_table` when the specifications must be read row by row, and `row_cards` when the items are not things you buy.

text.description: What this person said, in their own words. One remark, not a passage.

name.description: Who said it. The initials beside the quote are derived from this exact string: a Latin name takes the first letter of each of its first two words, a single Latin word takes its own first two letters, and a CJK name takes only its surname character.

role.description: Optional one line placing the speaker — their title, their organization, or both.

featured.description: Optional. Marks the one quote the page turns on: it is filled solid and its text is set to read against that fill. At most one quote in the set may set it.

quotes.description: 2-4 remarks side by side, each with its speaker, in the order they should be read left to right.

quote_wall.description: Sets 2-4 short remarks side by side, each with the speaker's initials, name, and role, so the page's claim is carried by several voices agreeing rather than one. Use quote_wall when the number of people saying it is the argument — customer voices, panel reactions, press notices. The test: does the point weaken if you keep only one of them? Use `blockquote` for a single remark set at full size, and `people_cards` when the page is about who these people are rather than what they said.

title.description: A name printed over the bridge.

note.description: A short line under the bar's label, such as the quantity it stands for: "3.187 吨", "+0.319 t" or "0.975 × 1.370 = 1.336 t".

emphasis.description: Marks a bar the page is about. Marked bars must sit next to each other and cannot be a total. The rest of the bridge recedes to grey.

emphasis_label.description: One line printed above the marked bars, saying what they add up to. Needs at least one item with emphasis: true.

text.description: One short line under the bar's label: what happens in that stretch, or why it matters.

emphasis.description: Marks the one bar the page is about. It keeps the lead colour and the other bars recede. At most one item.

icon.description: A symbol for the row, drawn before its label, such as coins or shield-check. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

period.description: How the bar's stretch reads in words, such as "第 16 至 18 个月" or "Months 16 to 18", printed with the row.

basis.description: What the stretch rests on, such as "pending" for work that happens only if a condition is met, or one of two paths still to be chosen. A stretch that is not settled is drawn as a dashed outline.

range.description: The stretch the axis runs over when it is longer than the bars, such as a whole 18-month plan whose bars cover parts of it: { "from": 0, "to": 18 }. Without it the axis runs from the first bar's start to the last bar's end. Every bar must lie inside it.

from.description: Where the axis starts, such as 0 for the start of a plan.

to.description: Where it ends, such as 18 for the end of an 18-month plan.

milestones.description: Up to two moments marked across the bars, each a line down the rows with a diamond and its label under them, such as a check the plan turns on: [{ "at": 8.5, "label": "Data gate, June 2027" }]. Each lies inside the axis.

at.description: Where the moment stands, on the same axis as the bars' start and end, such as 8.5 for the middle of the ninth month.

label.description: What happens then, printed by its mark under the bars, such as "数据闸门 · 2027 年 6 月" or "Data gate, June 2027".

bands.description: Up to two spans of the axis marked behind the bars, each tinted and named under the axis, such as the season a plan is built around: [{ "from": 8, "to": 12, "label": "演唱会季 6 至 9 月" }]. Each lies inside the axis (range, or the bars' own stretch), ends after it starts, and keeps clear of the other.

from.description: Where the span starts, on the same axis as the bars' start and end.

label.description: What the span is, printed under the axis, such as "演唱会季 6 至 9 月" or "Concert season, Jun to Sep".

label_every.description: Print every Nth column label from the first, such as 6 for a day's hours.

steps.description: Two to five named steps, lowest first, each cell coloured by the step its value falls in: [{ "max": 0.5, "label": "低谷", "short": "谷" }, { "label": "高峰" }]. Not with domain.

max.description: The step's highest value. The last step has none.

label.description: Its name in the key, such as "低谷" or "Off-peak".

short.description: A shorter name the cells print, such as "谷" or "Off".

bands.description: Up to two runs of columns marked across every row, each framed and named under the grid, such as the season a plan is built around: [{ "from": "6 月", "to": "9 月", "label": "2027 演唱会季 · 6 至 9 月" }]. from and to name two x_labels, from first, and two runs do not share a column.

from.description: The first column the run covers, written as its x_label, such as "6 月" or "Jun".

to.description: The last column it covers, written as its x_label, such as "9 月" or "Sep". The same as from for one column.

label.description: What the run is, printed under it, such as "2027 演唱会季 · 6 至 9 月" or "2027 season, Jun to Sep".

icon.description: A symbol before the run's name, such as sun.

title.description: A short name for the table, printed over it, such as "自由现金流" or "Free cash flow". A theme that sets it in a panel prints the title in the panel's title bar.

emphasis.description: Marks the one column the page is about, such as the figure no company has published: its header and cells are set bold in the emphasis colour and the column is outlined. At most one column.

icon.description: A symbol drawn before every cell of the column, such as circle-help on figures nobody has published. A left-aligned column only. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.
A symbol for the row, drawn at its start before the first cell, such as server or cloud. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

tag.description: What kind of row it is, in a word or two printed as a small tag at the start of the row's last cell, such as 倡导, 独立 or Independent, when the rows sort into a few kinds the reader should tell apart. Set quiet on a tag that says nothing in particular.

device.description: Frame shape to draw: "browser" (adds an optional address-bar `url`) or "phone" (no address bar).

url.description: Address-bar text shown in the browser window bar. Only valid when device is "browser".

device_mockup.description: Frames a product or app screenshot inside a real device (a browser window or a phone) so it reads as software that is actually running, not a flat picture. Use device_mockup for screenshots of a UI, dashboard, or app; keep plain photos, illustrations, and other non-screen images as `image`.

label.description: Short label shown inside the stage's node on the ring.

description.description: Optional short explanation shown outside the node, next to it.

items.description: 3-8 stages placed at equal steps around a closed ring, connected clockwise, the last stage arcing back to the first — author them in reading order.

cycle.description: Lays 3-8 stages out on a closed ring with arrow connectors, for a process that has no endpoint — it loops back to its own start (PDCA, a product lifecycle, a flywheel, a seasonal cycle). Use cycle when the last stage leads back into the first; use `flowchart` instead when the process reaches a real endpoint, even if it branches, since a loop forced through flowchart closes on a stray line.

name.description: Full name as written — the initials badge is derived from this exact string (deriveInitials, people-initials.ts): a Latin name takes the first letter of each of its first two words, a single Latin word takes its own first two letters, and a CJK name takes only its first character (surname), never two.

role.description: Optional one-line role, title, or topic shown under the name.

people.description: 2-12 people laid out on an equal-weight card grid (1-3 rows, sized by count), each card an initials badge (derived from name, no photo needed) plus name and optional role/org — author them in the reading order you want the grid to fill row-major.

people_cards.description: Lays 2-12 people out on an equal-weight card grid, each with a deterministic initials badge in place of a photo, for a page about *people*: a team roster, a speaker lineup, a judging panel, an author list. Use people_cards when every item names a person, and keep `row_cards`/`icon_cards` (at most 6 items) for anything else, such as features, milestones or topics, even with name/role/org-shaped fields.

center.description: The one concept every element relates to. Drawn inside the central node.

label.description: Short name of one related element.

description.description: Optional one-line explanation shown beside the label.

items.description: 3-6 peer elements arranged around the center. Order carries no meaning here — author them in whatever order reads best.

hub_spoke.description: One central concept with 3-6 peer elements attached to it, drawn as a hub with labelled spokes. Use hub_spoke when the elements are unordered and do not close a loop: they all relate to the center, not to each other. Use `steps` when the elements run in sequence, `cycle` when the last one leads back to the first, and `rings` when they nest inside one another.

value.description: Completion rate: "86%", "86" and "0.86" all read as 86 percent. A number and an optional trailing "%", nothing else.

label.description: What the rate measures.

detail.description: The amounts behind the rate, such as "11770 / 13000 亿元" or "¥1.18tn of ¥1.3tn", printed on a line under the label.

emphasis.description: Marks the one rate the page is about: its ring, figure and label take the emphasis colour. At most one.

progress_donuts.description: 2-6 completion rates, each drawn as a ring filled to its own percentage. Use progress_donuts when every value is a share of a whole — a completion rate, a coverage percentage, an attainment against target. Use `kpi_cards` when the values are absolute quantities or growth rates, and `chart` with chart_type gauge when a single rate is the whole message.

title.description: Name of this level.

value.description: The one number this level carries, written as it should read.

unit.description: Unit printed after the number, in smaller type.

note.description: Optional single line under the number.

items.description: 3-6 levels in ascending order, lowest first. The last one is drawn as the top step and carries the highlight.

staircase.description: 3-6 levels that climb, drawn as real stairs: every tread sits one riser above the one before it, and the top step is filled so the destination reads first. Use staircase when the levels differ in degree — maturity, tier, seniority — and the climb itself is the argument. Use `steps` when they follow one another in time, `chevron_process` when they are the stages of a pipeline, and `timeline` when each one has a date.

title.description: Name of this stage, two to six words.

text.description: Optional short note printed under the chevron, not inside it. It wraps to a second line when it needs one, and two lines is all it gets.

icon.description: A symbol for the stage, drawn at the top right of its chevron on the line of its number, such as id-card or badge-check. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

items.description: 3-6 stages in the order work passes through them. The last one is the destination and carries the fill.

chevron_process.description: 3-6 stages of one pipeline, drawn as interlocking chevrons that point at the next stage. Use chevron_process when work has to pass through every stage in order and the handover between them is the point. Use `steps` when each stage needs a paragraph of its own, `flowchart` when the path branches on a decision, `cycle` when the last stage feeds the first, and `staircase` when the stages climb rather than follow.

label.description: Who owns this lane — a team, a role, a system.

role.description: Optional second line under the lane name.

lanes.description: 2-4 lanes, top to bottom, in the order they should be read.

lane.description: The label of the lane this step happens in. Must match one of `lanes`.

title.description: What happens at this step.

detail.description: Optional single line inside the box — a duration, a count, an owner.

steps.description: 3-7 steps in the order work moves through them. Each step sits in exactly one lane.

handoff_note.description: One line about the handover, printed beside the first arrow that crosses lanes.

swimlane.description: One process running left to right across 2-4 lanes, one lane per role, so the moment work changes hands is visible. Use swimlane when who does each step is part of the argument. Use `steps` when one team does all of it, `flowchart` when the path branches on a decision, and `chevron_process` when the stages matter but their owners do not.

label.description: Name of this stage of the journey.

touchpoints.description: Up to 3 places the person meets you at this stage, each a short noun phrase.

action.description: What the person actually does here, in one line.

emotion.description: How this stage feels, 1 (worst) to 5 (best). The curve is drawn from these.

opportunity.description: What could be fixed here, in one line.

stages.description: 3-6 stages in the order the person passes through them.

row_labels.description: Names for the four rows. Omitted, each row prints the component's own word, in the script the stages are written in — write this only to say it differently.

journey_map.description: 3-6 stages of one person's journey, with what they meet, what they do, how it feels on a 1-5 curve, and what could be fixed. Use journey_map when the low point of the curve is the argument and the fix belongs beside it. Use `chevron_process` for the stages of a pipeline with no feeling attached, `swimlane` when the question is who does each step, and `timeline` when the stages carry dates.

question.description: The decision itself, written as the question being answered.

edge.description: The condition that leads down this branch — this is what makes it a decision.

title.description: Where this branch goes, named in a few words.

detail.description: Optional single line under the branch name.

edge.description: Label on the line into this outcome — a share, a probability, a condition.

title.description: The outcome itself, named in a few words.

detail.description: Optional single line on what this outcome costs or means.

value.description: The one number this outcome carries, written as it should read.

unit.description: Unit printed after the number, in smaller type.

recommended.description: Marks the one outcome the deck is arguing for. It is filled whole; at most one may be set.

outcomes.description: 2-3 outcomes this branch can end in.

branches.description: 2-3 paths out of the question, each with its own condition on the line.

decision_tree.description: One question, 2-3 paths out of it, and 2-3 outcomes down each path, with the condition written on every line. Use decision_tree when the reader has to see which condition sends them where, and what each ending costs. Use `flowchart` when the path has one thread with decisions along it, `steps` when there is no branching at all, and `comparison` when the endings sit side by side with no route into them.

kicker.description: Tiny line above the state name, in the deck's own language.

title.description: What this state is — a period, a version, a way of working.

kicker.description: Tiny line above the state name, in the deck's own language.

title.description: What this state is — a period, a version, a way of working.

to.description: Where things end up. This is the side that carries the fill.

label.description: What this row measures.

icon.description: A symbol before the row's name.

note.description: A short line under the name, such as where the figures come from: "CNESA estimate".

from.description: The value in the starting state, written as it should read.

to.description: The value in the ending state, written as it should read.

unit.description: Unit printed after both values, in smaller type.

change.description: The move itself, in the words the deck uses for it.

tag.description: What this measure is, in a few words printed as a small tag after its values, such as 新增 or New. Set quiet on a tag that says nothing changed.

emphasis.description: Marks the one measure the page is about: its row is set apart and its tag fills in the emphasis colour. At most one row.

rows.description: 3-6 measures, the same ones on both sides, in the order they should be read.

label_column.description: The header over the measures' names, such as "指标" or "Measure".

span.description: What separates the two states — a duration, a release, a decision. Printed under the arrow.

from_to.description: Two states of the same thing, measured on the same rows, with an arrow between them. Use from_to when every row has a value on both sides and the move between them is the argument. Use `comparison` when the two sides are different things rather than the same thing twice, `kpi_cards` when one column of numbers stands on its own, and `steps` when what happens in between matters more than the endpoints.

name.description: The person or unit at the top.

role.description: One short line under the name.

name.description: The person or unit this node names.

role.description: One short line under the name.

children.description: The nodes reporting to this one. Omit it and the branch is itself a bottom node.

name.description: The person or unit this node names.

role.description: One short line under the name.

children.description: The nodes directly under the root, left to right in the order they should read.

org_tree.description: A reporting structure three levels deep at most: one root, 2-6 branches under it, and an optional row of nodes under each branch, capped at 8 bottom nodes in total. Use org_tree when the lines mean 'reports to'. Use `issue_tree` when they mean 'breaks down into', `rings` when the levels nest one inside another, `pyramid` when each level supports the one above it, and `people_cards` when the names are peers with no lines between them.

question.description: The question the whole tree answers, written as a question.

children_column.description: The header over the sub-points, saying what they are, such as "各留一条独立的路" or "What we do about each". Only with sub-points.

label.description: One hypothesis the question splits into.

note.description: One line saying how much of the question this branch accounts for.

icon.description: A symbol for the hypothesis, drawn before its label, such as globe or database. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

emphasis.description: Mark the one branch the page argues for. It is filled solid instead of outlined.

children.description: The sub-points under this hypothesis. Omit it and the hypothesis is the end of its own line.

label.description: One testable sub-point, short enough to read in a single line.

branches.description: The hypotheses the question splits into, in the order they should be read down the page.

issue_tree.description: A question broken into 2-4 hypotheses and their sub-points, three levels deep at most and capped at 8 end points, drawn left to right. Use issue_tree when a line means 'breaks down into' and the branches are meant to be mutually exclusive. Use `org_tree` when a line means 'reports to', and `flowchart` when each branch is a decision taken on a condition.

label.description: What this level is called.

note.description: One line explaining the level, printed in the legend beside the drawing.

tone.description: What kind of news the level is, its band painted in the theme's own colour for it: "danger" for the level to guard most, such as personal data, "warning" for one to handle with care, "success" for one that is safe. Give every level a tone or none.

layers.description: The levels from the top down. The first entry is the apex.

pyramid.description: 3-6 levels stacked into a pyramid, apex first, each level optionally explained in a legend beside the drawing. Use pyramid when each level rests on the one below it — a claim over its evidence, a rank over the ranks that hold it. Use `rings` when the levels nest one inside another, `architecture` when each level holds the parts of a system, `steps` when they are performed in order, and `row_cards` when they are peers.

above.description: What everyone already says, printed in the tip above the waterline.

below.description: What nobody raises, printed in the submerged mass under the waterline.

waterline.description: Name for the line itself, printed at its left end.

above_label.description: What the visible band is, printed to the right of the tip.

below_label.description: What the hidden band is, printed to the right of the mass.

iceberg.description: A berg with 1-2 stated items above the waterline and 3-6 unstated ones below it, both printed inside the silhouette. Use iceberg when the argument is that the visible part is the small part. Use `comparison` when the two sets are peers being weighed, and `pyramid` when the levels support one another.

goal.description: The one outcome the pillars hold up. Printed across the beam.

title.description: What this pillar is called.

value.description: The one figure this pillar is measured by.

unit.description: Unit printed small beside the figure.

pillars.description: The columns holding the beam up, left to right. One title and one figure each.

base.description: The shared footing every pillar stands on. Printed across the base slab.

pillar_model.description: A beam carrying one goal, 2-5 pillars each with a title and a figure, and a base slab naming the shared footing. Use pillar_model when the goal only holds if every pillar holds. Use `icon_cards` when the items are simply parallel, `steps` when they run in order, and `pyramid` when each level rests on the next.

label.description: What happens at this link of the chain.

value.description: The share or figure this link carries.

unit.description: Unit printed small beside the figure.

emphasis.description: Mark the one link the page is about. It is filled solid instead of outlined.

primary.description: The primary activities in the order value passes through them.

label.description: What this supporting function is called.

note.description: One line naming what it actually provides.

support.description: The functions that span every link rather than sitting at one of them.

margin.description: The wedge closing the right end of the chain.

label.description: What the closing wedge is called.

value_chain.description: 3-6 interlocking primary links in a row, 2-4 supporting bands spanning above them, and an optional closing wedge. Use value_chain when the question is where along the chain value is made. Use `steps` when only the order matters, and `sankey` when a quantity splits and merges between stages.

criteria.description: 3-5 criteria, one column each, in the order they should be read.

label.description: The option this row scores.

items.description: How far this option meets this criterion: 0 empty, 25 a quarter, 50 half, 75 three quarters, 100 full.

scores.description: One score per criterion, in the same order as `criteria`.

total.description: Optional summary figure for the row, printed at its end.

highlight.description: Marks the one option the page argues for. The row is filled solid.

legend.description: Print a key under the grid naming the empty, half and full circle. Off by default.

labels.description: Header and key wording override. A missing key falls back to the grid's own word, which is Chinese when the criteria and option names are written in Chinese and English otherwise.

harvey_balls.description: 3-6 options scored against 3-5 shared criteria, each score drawn as a circle filled none, a quarter, half, three quarters or full. Use harvey_balls when the scores are a judgement in five steps and the reader's question is which option has no weak column. Use heatmap when the values are continuous numbers whose spread across two dimensions is the message, data_table when any figure has to be read exactly, and comparison for qualitative attributes with no shared scale.

labels.description: Column header override. A missing key falls back to the card's own word, which is Chinese when the goals and figures are written in Chinese and English otherwise.

label.description: The goal being scored.

target.description: What was promised, written the way it should print.

actual.description: What was reached, written the way it should print.

gap.description: The distance between the two, sign included.

status.description: Verdict for the row: on_track, watch, or off_track. Chooses the tone, not the wording.

status_label.description: The verdict in the author's own words. Left out, the card's own word for this status prints beside the dot, in the script the card is written in.

rows.description: 3-8 goals, one row each, in the order they should be read.

note.description: Optional line under the grid: how the gap is measured, or where the numbers came from.

scorecard.description: 3-8 goals, each with its target, what was reached, the gap between them, and a verdict. Use scorecard when the page's question is which promises were kept and by how much. Use data_table when the numbers are reported without a verdict, kpi_cards when one figure owns the page, and progress_donuts when every value is a completion rate.

filled.description: How many of the ten figures are filled: 0 to 10.

label.description: What the filled figures did, in one line.

caption.description: Optional line above the label naming the ten: who or what the row counts.

highlight.description: Marks the one row the page argues from. Its label is set in the strong ink.

rows.description: 1-3 rows, each counting out of ten.

pictogram.description: 1-3 proportions, each drawn as ten figures with some of them filled. Use pictogram when a rate should land as a countable number of people rather than a percentage. Use progress_donuts when the rate itself is the subject, kpi_cards when one figure owns the page, and chart for a series over time.

text.description: One word or short phrase, as it should be set.

weight.description: Which of the four sizes this word is set in: 4 largest, 1 smallest.

words.description: 8-20 words, each with its own weight. Where a word lands is decided by its weight and then by the word itself, so authoring order changes nothing.

word_cloud.description: 8-20 words set in four sizes, packed from the middle outward by weight and then alphabetically, no word turned on its side. Use word_cloud when the point is which words keep coming back. Use chart when the counts must be read, bullets when the findings are sentences, and tag_row for a line of labels that carry no weight against each other.

label.description: Short name of one set. Drawn beside its own circle.

sets.description: 2-3 overlapping sets, one short label each. Set order runs clockwise from the top.

center.description: Short name of the region every set shares — the point of the drawing, printed on the overlap.

venn.description: Two or three overlapping circles whose shared region is the message. Use venn when the argument is that something sits in more than one set at once. Use `comparison` when the sides are weighed against each other rather than overlapping, `matrix` when two dimensions cross into quadrants, and `rings` when each set contains the one inside it.

effect.description: The result being explained. Drawn in the head at the end of the spine.

label.description: Short name of one cause category.

causes.description: 2-3 specific causes under this category, each a short line.

ribs.description: 4-6 cause categories, drawn alternately above and below the spine in the order written.

fishbone.description: One result and the four to six categories of cause behind it, drawn as a spine with slanted ribs. Use fishbone for a diagnosis: the effect is known and the page sorts why it happened. Use `flowchart` when the boxes are steps that lead somewhere, `hub_spoke` when the elements relate to a centre rather than explain it, and `row_cards` when the categories carry prose instead of short causes.

title.description: What the axis measures — the dimension, never one of its values.

low.description: Short name of the low end.

high.description: Short name of the high end.

x_axis.description: The horizontal dimension and the words at each end.

title.description: What the axis measures — the dimension, never one of its values.

low.description: Short name of the low end.

high.description: Short name of the high end.

y_axis.description: The vertical dimension and the words at each end.

quadrants.description: Optional name for each of the four quadrants. All four or none.

label.description: Short name of one plotted subject.

x.description: Position along the horizontal axis, 0 at the low end and 100 at the high end.

y.description: Position along the vertical axis, 0 at the low end and 100 at the high end.

emphasis.description: Marks the one subject the page is about.

points.description: 4-10 plotted subjects, each with a position on both axes.

positioning_map.description: Subjects plotted on two continuous dimensions, with named ends and optional quadrant names. Use positioning_map when where each subject sits — and how far it is from the others — is the argument. Use `matrix` when the two dimensions are categories rather than scales, `comparison` when the subjects are weighed attribute by attribute, and `chart` with chart_type scatter when the numbers themselves are the subject.

label.description: What this term is — the name the reader reads it by.

value.description: Optional figure for the term, printed large.

note.description: Optional single line under the term.

icon.description: A symbol for the term, drawn at the top of its panel, such as route or hospital. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

operands.description: 2-3 terms added together, in the order they should be read.

label.description: What this term is — the name the reader reads it by.

value.description: Optional figure for the term, printed large.

note.description: Optional single line under the term.

icon.description: A symbol for the term, drawn at the top of its panel, such as route or hospital. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

result.description: What the terms add up to.

excluded.description: What the result leaves out on purpose, drawn under the equation in a dashed outline with its figure struck through, such as { "label": "先不做", "value": "核心城区的餐饮高峰单", "note": "它排在放行顺序最后" } or { "label": "Not yet", "value": "Lunch-hour food in the city core" }. Give it a value: the value is what is struck.

label.description: What this term is — the name the reader reads it by.

value.description: Optional figure for the term, printed large.

note.description: Optional single line under the term.

icon.description: A symbol for the term, drawn at the top of its panel, such as route or hospital. Run `pptwise icons` for the names.

concept_equation.description: Two or three terms adding up to one result, drawn as panels joined by a plus and an equals sign. Use concept_equation when the argument is that these things together produce that thing. Use `icon_cards` when the items are peers that produce nothing between them, `steps` when one leads to the next, and `kpi_cards` when the figures stand on their own.

center.description: What the whole is. Drawn in the hub.

label.description: Short name of one part.

value.description: Optional short figure printed under the name.

emphasis.description: Marks the one part the page is about.

segments.description: 4-8 equal parts of the whole, drawn clockwise from the top in the order written.

segmented_wheel.description: One whole cut into four to eight equal parts around a hub, with one part able to be marked. Use segmented_wheel when the parts together are the whole and none of them leads to the next. Use `cycle` when the last part returns to the first, `hub_spoke` when the elements hang off the centre rather than divide it, and `chart` with chart_type pie when the parts are unequal shares.

title.description: What this side is called, in the deck's own language.

label.description: The point itself, in one short line.

note.description: Optional single line of evidence under the point.

title.description: What this side is called, in the deck's own language.

label.description: The point itself, in one short line.

note.description: Optional single line of evidence under the point.

verdict.description: The call the page makes after weighing both sides. Required: a weighing with no verdict is a shrug.

pros_cons.description: One proposal weighed in two columns and closed with a verdict. Use pros_cons when both sides are about the same proposal and the page has to land somewhere. Use `comparison` when the two columns are two different subjects, and `verdict_banner` when the conclusion is the whole page.

kind.description: "discontinuity": an outcome that jumps where a running variable crosses a cutoff, two fitted lines over scattered points with the jump between them marked, as a regression discontinuity design reads. "difference_in_differences": two groups' trends running side by side until an event, then the treated one leaving the path it would have kept, drawn dashed, as a difference-in-differences design reads.

at.description: What stands at the dashed line: the cutoff, such as "法定年龄" or "Statutory age", or the event, such as "新政施行" or "Reform starts".

x_title.description: What runs along the bottom, such as "年龄", "时间", "Age" or "Time". An arrow is set after it.

y_title.description: What the outcome is, set at the top of the upright axis, such as "在业" or "In work".

effect.description: discontinuity only: what the jump is read as, printed beside its arrow, such as "跳跃 = 效应" or "Jump = effect".

groups.description: difference_in_differences only, and required there: the treated group and then its control, each named at the end of its line, such as ["新规队列", "相邻旧规队列"] or ["New-rule cohorts", "Neighbouring cohorts"].

direction.description: Which way the outcome moves: at the cutoff, or the treated line after the event against the path it would have kept. Omitted, "up".

sketch.description: A schematic, with no figures, of how an effect is told apart from everything else: an outcome that jumps at a cutoff (a regression discontinuity), or a treated group's trend leaving its control's after an event (a difference-in-differences). Use sketch to show the shape of an argument a study rests on. Use `chart` when there are real figures to plot.
